short: The UAE has no federal AI statute. The binding AI-specific rule is DIFC Data Protection Regulation 10, in force since 1 September 2023, on top of the federal data protection law; an Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority was approved on 14 June 2026.
title: UAE AI Laws
subtitle: No federal AI act: DIFC Regulation 10, the federal PDPL and a new AI and Data Authority
body_html:
Status at a glance

No federal AI act; data protection law binds. The UAE has no horizontal AI statute. The one binding AI-specific rule is in the Dubai International Financial Centre: Regulation 10 of the DIFC Data Protection Regulations, on personal data processed through autonomous and semi-autonomous systems, in force since 1 September 2023. Outside the free zones, the federal data protection law applies. On 14 June 2026 Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid approved the establishment of the Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority, reporting directly to the Cabinet, with a mandate to propose AI and data policies, laws and strategies; it consolidates the Office of Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications, the Digital Government Sector of the Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority, and the UAE Data Office. It is an authority, not a statute. Verified on 25 October 2026 against the DIFC, the Dubai Media Office and u.ae.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberPublishedIn force
DIFC Data Protection Regulations, Regulation 10Consolidated Version No. 2, under DIFC Law No. 5 of 20201 September 20231 September 2023; amendments and a new Regulation 11 consulted on 18 June to 18 July 2026
DIFC Data Protection LawDIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (consolidated July 2025)2020In force

Who regulates and enforces

  • DIFC Commissioner of Data Protection: administers the DIFC law and regulations, including Regulation 10 certification.
  • UAE Data Office: the federal data regulator, now consolidated into the Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority.
  • Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority: reports to the Cabinet; proposes policies, laws and strategies and sets data and AI standards for federal entities.

Scope and reach

The DIFC Data Protection Law applies to a controller or processor incorporated in the DIFC, wherever the processing happens, and to processing in the DIFC as part of stable arrangements (Art. 6(3)). There is no trigger based on where users are. Regulation 10 defines systems, deployers, operators and providers, and treats a deployer as a controller and an operator as a processor (Regs 10.1.1 and 10.3.4).

Core obligations

  • Clear and explicit notice when an autonomous system is first used, describing its purposes, outputs, design principles and certifications (Reg 10.2.2(a) and (b)).
  • On request, evidence of audit or certification, human-intervention design, risk and impact assessments, and a register of use cases (Reg 10.2.2(c) to (g)).
  • Design to be ethical, fair, transparent, secure and accountable (Reg 10.3.1); no commercial use unless purposes are defined or approved by humans and the system meets certification requirements (Reg 10.3.2).
  • High-risk processing only with the Commissioner's certification and an Autonomous Systems Officer (Reg 10.3.3).

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Listed contraventions of the DIFC Data Protection Law, for example Arts. 9 to 12 and 14(2) at USD 50,000 and the data subject rights in Arts. 33 to 38 at USD 100,000USD 25,000 to USD 100,000 per contraventionDIFC Law No. 5 of 2020, Art. 62(2) and Schedule 2DIFC Commissioner of Data Protection
Any contravention, including of Regulation 10 (which sets no fine of its own)A general fine "not limited to the amounts specified in Schedule 2"DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020, Art. 62(3)DIFC Commissioner of Data Protection

What is coming next

  • The final amended Regulation 10 and a new Regulation 11, after DIFC Consultation Paper No. 3 of 2026 (18 June to 18 July 2026); no date published.
  • Any legislative proposal from the Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority.

The layers between the Charter and the free zones

Federal policy is set by the National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031 and the UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence of June 2024, twelve principles on safety, transparency and human oversight that bind nobody but are the reference public procurement and the ministries' AI chief executives apply; the UAE Council for AI and, since April 2025, a Regulatory Intelligence Office that uses AI to track legislation sit beside them. The Authority approved on 14 June 2026 will be led by the Minister of State for AI, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications; Morgan Lewis notes that its most immediate effect for mainland businesses is to decide who regulates the federal PDPL, since the UAE Data Office it absorbs had never been fully established. Whether the Authority has issued any rule of its own was not found. On the mainland the binding statutes remain Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021, the PDPL, in force since 2 January 2022 and covering profiling and automated processing, and Federal Decree-Law No. 34 of 2021 on rumours and cybercrime, which reaches AI-enabled fraud and fabricated content; the Penal Code applies in the free zones too. Mainland UAE is a civil law jurisdiction with no reported AI case law.

The one sector with AI-specific binding expectations is finance. On 11 February 2026 the Central Bank of the UAE published a Guidance Note on Consumer Protection and Responsible Adoption of AI and Machine Learning addressed to all licensed financial institutions, banks, finance companies, exchange houses, insurers and payment providers. It requires an inventory of every AI model with purpose, risk rating and metadata, aligned with the 2022 Model Management Standards; board-level governance; consumer disclosure; and accountability for third-party AI, which an institution cannot treat as the vendor's problem. Hadef and Partners read the note as forming part of supervisory dialogue, and a failure to align can be treated as a governance shortfall under article 14 of Federal Decree-Law No. 48 of 2023 on insurance. It runs alongside the new Central Bank law, Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025, in force 16 September 2025 with a regularisation deadline of 16 September 2026, and the 2021 joint Enabling Technologies Guidelines of the CBUAE, the Securities and Commodities Authority, the DFSA and the ADGM FSRA.

In the free zones, DIFC Regulation 10 covers every DIFC entity, not only financial firms, and is supported by a 2023 guidance note from the Commissioner of Data Protection; the DIFC has since announced an AI-native strategy. The ADGM has no equivalent to Regulation 10, but its Data Protection Regulations 2021 apply to any automated processing and its Office of Data Protection has issued guidance. HSF Kramer's tracker, which this site could read where the Central Bank's own site returned 403, is the source for the sector material above.

Last verified

4 November 2026, against the sources above. The Central Bank guidance note of 11 February 2026, the new Central Bank law dates, the Charter and the Authority's leadership are as Morgan Lewis, CMS and HSF Kramer report them, not read on centralbank.ae or u.ae, which answered 403, and are reported rather than verified. Still left out: the federal PDPL's penalties.
